value.body: A three-year postgraduate degree in Ayurveda taken after BAMS — MD (Ayurveda) in medical subjects or MS (Ayurveda) in surgical ones. Subjects include Kayachikitsa (medicine), Panchakarma, Shalya Tantra (surgery), Shalakya Tantra (eye and ENT), Prasuti Tantra & Stri Roga (obstetrics and gynaecology), Kaumarabhritya (paediatrics), Dravyaguna and Rasa Shastra. It is regulated by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM).

items.label: Entrance exam
items.note: Conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA)

items.label: All-India counselling
items.note: Ayush Admissions Central Counselling Committee; state-quota seats go through state counselling

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BAMS degree with completed internship, then a qualifying AIAPGET score. AACCC counsels the all-India quota (15% of seats in government and aided colleges) and seats in central universities, national institutes and deemed universities; the remaining seats go through state counselling.

value.title: At a glance
items: Your AIAPGET rank largely decides both the subject and the college you get.
Fees at government colleges are much lower than at private and deemed colleges.
It leads to specialist practice, teaching in Ayurveda colleges (where a PG is required for faculty posts) and research.
A PhD in Ayurveda (Ayurveda Vachaspati) is the next academic step.
